Special Agents Charles Kunkel and Maurice Miller wrote this Secret Service report in November and December 1963. It is numbered CO-2-34,030 and comes from the Dallas office. Its subject is protective research into the assassination of President Kennedy: the service's own study of how its protection had failed.

Protective research was the branch meant to learn from threats before they succeeded. After Dallas, it studied the worst failure in the service's history. Kunkel and Miller's report belongs to the first weeks of that reckoning. It preserves the service examining itself while the Warren Commission was still being formed, a primary record of an agency asking what it had missed.
govdocs-nsarchive-Briefing_Book_russia-p:
In May 2016 the Archive published Anatoly Chernyaev's diary for 1976, in English for the first time. The edition includes Chernyaev's own later edits and a postscript by the author. That makes the volume two texts at once: the diary as written, and the diarist revisiting himself.

Chernyaev observed the Soviet leadership from inside the Central Committee across the Brezhnev years. His diaries became famous for their candor about colleagues and about his own disillusion. A year volume like 1976, before the famous Gorbachev period, shows the observer's eye already trained. Readers following the whole diary series can watch his judgments sharpen year by year.
